<description>
An ipc client can pass any timeout to `waitTipChanged`, but the code assumes it is never negative:

```
Assume(timeout >= 0ms); // No internal callers should use a negative timeout
```

On debug builds, a negative or NaN timeout fails this check and aborts the node. I reproduced this with a timeout of -1.0.

On release builds the check is skipped. Negative values are clamped to zero, but NaN is not, because every comparison with NaN is false. It ends up as the deadline passed to `wait_until`.

`waitNext` has no Assume, but it also doesn't check its timeout. A NaN timeout waits one extra fee tick (about one second) before returning.

We now treat negative and NaN timeouts as zero in both methods, removes the Assume, and documents the behavior in the interface. The functional test covers negative and NaN timeouts for both methods.

I'm not aware of any client that sends these values (sv2-tp, for example, requires an interval of at least one second), so this is hardening against bad input from ipc clients.

_This is similar to #36520, which handles invalid arguments to the Chain interface for the same reason._

Links

- https://ipcbugs.ofsky.org/bugs/bitcoin-2026-wait-timeout-assume/
</description>

<commits>
e1bee89d32 mining: handle negative and NaN waitTipChanged timeouts

Wait timeouts can come from an IPC client, so they should not be
checked with Assume. Negative and Nan values aborted debug builds
in waitTipChanged, and NaN also passed the clamps in release builds

Treat negative and Nan timeouts as zero in waitTipChanged and
waitNext, document and add functional test
</commits>
